findings.title: Compiled aliased transform readers can dereference removed buffers before the new face-head refusals
findings.evidence: The new guards cover draw_*_faces but omit 3dtrans.c pointer aliases. draw_wbuffered_3d_object calls transform_flat_3d_object, transform_3d_object or their unclipped variants before its guarded face calls. Those compiled functions assign points=object->points and then read points->x or points[]. Surface transforms also dereference the detached current_object_3d_surface_point_list alias, and illuminate_3d_object_surface reads that alias before the surface transform. Both files are ordinary source-list members under the active non-OGRE branch. Unlike obsolete 3denv.c, these bodies are not globally #if 0. Retaining true point counts makes their loops execute while the new loader makes their pointers NULL.
findings.required_change: Add named unsupported-reader guards at the actual aliased reader heads or prove a dominating guarded visual entry before every detached-buffer access. Cover whole-object, flat/unclipped and surface transform families and the surface-illumination point-reference alias. Preserve original diagnostic profiles. No renderer or geometry service is required, and a downstream face guard is insufficient.
findings.scope: Source-backed unsafe path, not a claim that the tested boot or short campaign invokes rendering. Current happy paths do not establish global dormancy or safe refusal for these compiled routes.

findings.title: New skipped/streamed regions assume successful I/O and can silently lose the claimed alignment or validation
findings.evidence: Every introduced fseek return is ignored. The new polygon streaming loop validates only got bytes but subtracts the requested chunk even when fread returned fewer bytes, so a missing polygon record can leave eech_polygon_face_invalid false and count as validated. It then continues subsequent metadata/texture reads. This is a defect in the new stream logic, independent of broader inherited unchecked header reads.
findings.required_change: Check the newly introduced seek results and require complete polygon chunks, with bounded fail-closed handling before treating the stream as aligned/validated or continuing consequences. Keep the successful read/texture-override/invalid-polygon phase ordering for valid supported files. No whole legacy-loader redesign or new asset policy is requested.
findings.scope: Valid verified retail files in the supplied runs do not exercise these errors. Do not infer malformed/truncated-file support from happy-path byte equality.

findings.title: Horizon witness strictness does not enforce the complete C grammar, coherence or Engine-owned stop cause
findings.evidence: The model-host line is checked only by a catalogue/scene prefix, so missing remaining fields or garbage suffix can pass. Integer parsing permits values outside the declared producer domains, and metadata_rows greater than rows can pass residency. A refusal is accepted by marker/operation substrings anywhere in the first line; the scripted healthy GUARD is bare host-model text, not the actual Engine-owned fatal prefix, so quoted tags or a generic callback/setup error can satisfy the witness. The actual CCC primary error is genuine; this finding concerns false acceptance of damaged evidence, not invalidating the measured actual failure.
findings.required_change: Reuse the exact existing C counter-field grammar, declare/check finite producer domains and row/count coherence, and require the actual once-only Engine-owned first-line object.geometry cause for this operation. Add finite coherent-positive-first damaged forms for missing/trailing first-row fields, impossible counts and bare/quoted/wrong-prefix causes. Preserve checked exclusive output and final closure. Correct the comment claiming feature absence is known before boot: capability methods are checked only after boot. Describe uncached refusal as before TGA/geometry work, without denying the earlier cached-.bin lookup.
findings.scope: Driver/test/prose correction; no new physical oracle, audio/UI product or broad trace framework.
